title: Viticulture Economic Profile and  Viticulture Sector Business Insight Report (West Sussex)  - AWARD
description:
The Rural West Sussex Partnership is an informal economic partnership between The South Downs National Park Authority, West Sussex County Council, Arun District Council, Chichester District Council, Horsham District Council and Mid-Sussex District Council. Its primary role is to champion and support the rural economy across rural West Sussex. 
      Rural West Sussex Partnership (RWSP) identified the viticulture sector as a project topic for the 2022-2023 year.  
      In 2021 the South Downs National Park Authority Viticulture Growth Impact Assessment was produced which illustrated the rapid scale of growth of the viticulture sector in the National Park with a 90% increase in vineyard coverage in the South Downs National Park (SDNP) since 2016. There are now approximately 65 vineyards across West Sussex.
      Following the recently commissioned East Sussex Community Renewal Fund (CRF) viticulture project and the production of the Wine Tourism Investment Implementation Plan for Sussex 2022 to 2028 and accompanying Technical Report, RWSP wish to commission the production of both a Viticulture Economic Profile and a Viticulture Business Insight Report for West Sussex.
      This project is to be a complementary study to the CRF funded research undertaken in East Sussex. 
      This invitation to quote is for both the profile and insight report, as detailed below.

awardedSupplier: Centre of Economics and Business Research

title: Crawley, Horsham, Mid Sussex and Mole Valley Electoral Print and Mail - AWARD
description:
Crawley Borough Council (lead procuring authority), Horsham District Council, Mid Sussex District Council and Mole Valley District Council each require a long term agreement, commencing 1st April 2024, for the provision of electoral print services.
      
      Each Participating Authority's contract will include for all the printing requirements of each Council's elections department, including but not limited to the poll cards and ballot papers for elections, the annual canvass exercises and for some Councils the Household notification letters.
      
      The appointed supplier will also be responsible for sourcing the materials to be printed on (card/paper etc.) and will be responsible for overseeing the posting/mailing requirements. It is anticipated that the postal element will be subcontracted by the appointed supplier but they will remain responsible for managing and overseeing this element.
      
      The appointed supplier must be capable of integrating with each Council's Election Management System; both their current system and their future system in the event Councils change their systems during the lifetime of their contracts.
      
      Each participating authority requires a contract lasting six years, up to 31st March 2030, with no extension options built in. This tender will have four independently awardable lots (one for each Council's contract).
